headline: OpenAI and Anthropic have hired several former Trump administration officials as they try to win trust in Washington.
score_reason: Curator score kept; facts support the story but it is influence-seeking, not a policy change.
importance_line: What changed: both AI labs are adding insiders from an administration that controls federal purchasing, export controls and supply-chain designations, which affects policymakers and rival firms, but hiring shows effort to gain influence, not any change in policy.
summary: CNBC reports, as relayed by Quartz on Yahoo Finance, that the two AI companies have together hired at least five former Trump administration officials this year, including Anthropic board member Chris Liddell and OpenAI's Dean Ball, who helped shape the administration's AI Action Plan. According to the report, the companies know the administration has many levers over their business, from government purchasing to export controls, and a federal appeals court ruled in September that the Pentagon had properly labelled Anthropic a supply-chain risk.
notes: CNBC page blocked (403); facts read in Quartz's summary on Yahoo Finance, which credits CNBC. Link is the CNBC original.
